 Advertisement Early voting, competitive races: What to know about the 2026 midterm elections in 8 charts
 Advertisement Updated: 3:00 AM PST Nov 1, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Damali Ramirez Data Researcher/Curator Annie Jennemann Data Journalist Early voting, competitive races: What to know about the 2026 midterm elections in 8 charts
 Updated: 3:00 AM PST Nov 1, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Damali Ramirez Data Researcher/Curator Annie Jennemann Data Journalist WASHINGTON — Voters across the country will decide which political party will gain or retain control of the U.S. Senate and House of Representatives, as well as the governorships in several states.
 The Get the Facts Data Team compiled a list of charts showing what to know about the 2026 midterm elections and the top issues voters are concerned about.
 Advertisement How many voters have cast an early ballot?
 More than 52 million ballots were cast early this election, either in person or by mail, according to the latest data from the University of Florida Election Lab. Early voting data is not election results, and therefore it's not yet known which candidate will win their races. 
 Some states with competitive races, like Texas, Georgia, Tennessee and North Carolina, have seen high early turnout. 
 In Texas, early ballots cast in person or by mail already made up more than 80% of the total votes for the state's 2022 midterm election as of Friday. Texas has a close, competitive Senate race between Democrat James Talarico and Republican Ken Paxton. 
 The Cook Political Report’s CPR Race Ratings identified 76 competitive races as of Oct. 30: 11 for the Senate, 53 for the House and 12 for state governor.
 The governor races in Kansas, Nevada and Georgia were rated as toss-ups, meaning the race could go either way.
 The Cook Political Report rated 11 Senate races as competitive, with seven of those being toss-ups. In order to gain control of the Senate, Democrats need to flip a net of four seats held by Republicans.
 Republicans currently hold a slim majority in the House of Representatives, with 218 seats. Democrats hold 214 House seats and would need a net gain of at least three seats to secure a majority. 
 Eighteen races in the House were considered toss-ups, including nine involving Republican incumbents.
 Some of these House races became competitive after states redrew their congressional districts in mid-decade redistricting.
 Florida’s 22nd district became an open seat after Democratic Rep. Lois Frankel’s district was redrawn as the 23rd district. Democrat Pia Dandiya and Republican Casey Askar are competing for the seat, which was rated a toss-up.
 What concerns do voters have?
 The economy, healthcare and the war in Iran were among the top issues voters said mattered the most in this midterm election, according to the latest Gallup poll . 
 A gallon of regular gas now averages $4.20 a gallon, up nearly 35% from when President Donald Trump took office. Diesel cost $3.63 a gallon at the start of Trump’s second term. It now costs $6.32, about 74% more. 
 The rise is partly due to higher oil prices amid uncertainty in the Middle East. The war in Iran has disrupted global oil supplies, affecting how much consumers pay at the pump.
 With energy prices higher, inflation has increased in the U.S. The latest report showed inflation was up 3.7% in September compared with the year prior. 
 In April 2025, the stock market plummeted when Trump announced sweeping tariffs for all trading partners, but it has since bounced back. The Dow Jones Industrial Average has risen by 20% since Trump’s second term began.
